court: District Court of Appeal of Florida

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must have authority to dissolve marriage and enter support/custody orders.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must have jurisdiction over each party to impose monetary and parenting obligations.

issues.label: Venue and residency requirements
issues.why: Florida dissolution requires statutory residency and proper venue.

issues.label: Date of separation significance
issues.why: Separation date controls retroactivity, classification of obligations, and potential valuation issues.

issues.label: Child is minor
issues.why: Court must confirm minor status to set support and parenting terms through majority.

issues.label: Parenting plan required
issues.why: A compliant parenting plan must be established under Florida law.

issues.label: Time-sharing schedule
issues.why: Court must set/approve timesharing in the child’s best interests.

issues.label: Best interests findings
issues.why: Parenting determinations require consideration of statutory best-interest factors.

issues.label: Ultimate decision-making authority
issues.why: Court must justify any grant of ultimate decision-making based on statutory criteria and evidence.

issues.label: Shared parental responsibility
issues.why: Court must decide shared vs sole responsibility and make required findings if limiting a parent.

issues.label: Health insurance for child
issues.why: Court must allocate responsibility for providing/maintaining health coverage if available/affordable.

issues.label: Uninsured medical expenses allocation
issues.why: Court must apportion uncovered medical/dental/vision costs between parents.

issues.label: HSA treatment and credits
issues.why: Court must determine whether HSA contributions/withdrawals are child-related and how to allocate/credit them.

issues.label: Extracurricular expenses allocation
issues.why: Court must decide whether and how extracurricular costs are shared and credited.

issues.label: Child support guideline calculation
issues.why: Court must compute support using statutory guidelines and include required inputs.

issues.label: Imputation of income
issues.why: Court must decide whether to impute income based on capacity vs actual earnings.

issues.label: Gross vs net income determinations
issues.why: Court must correctly define each party’s income and permissible deductions for support.

issues.label: Bonuses and variable pay
issues.why: Court must address inclusion/averaging of bonuses/commissions in income.

issues.label: Tax filing status effects
issues.why: Separate vs joint returns may affect net income and support calculations.

issues.label: Dependency exemption allocation
issues.why: Court should decide which parent claims the child for tax purposes and any conditions.

issues.label: Retroactive child support
issues.why: Court must determine retroactivity start date (e.g., separation/filing) and compute arrears/credits.

issues.label: Temporary support credits
issues.why: Court must reconcile temporary child support payments against final retroactive obligation.

issues.label: Overpayment recoupment method
issues.why: Court must decide how any overage paid is credited (offset, arrears reduction, or future credit).

issues.label: Arrears computation accuracy
issues.why: Court must ensure the math for arrears/credits is correct and supported by evidence.

issues.label: Deviation from guidelines
issues.why: If deviating, court must make written findings supporting deviation and amount.

issues.label: Marital standard of living
issues.why: Standard of living informs support and alimony considerations.

issues.label: Alimony statute applicability
issues.why: Court must apply the correct alimony framework given current Florida law and case timing.

issues.label: Alimony type authorized
issues.why: Court must ensure the chosen form (lump sum/durational) is legally permissible under the circumstances.

issues.label: Threshold for alimony award
issues.why: Court must find recipient need and payor ability to pay.

issues.label: Durational alimony prerequisites
issues.why: Court must determine eligibility and required findings for durational support.

issues.label: Lump-sum alimony basis
issues.why: Court must justify lump-sum structure (equitable distribution support, security, or special circumstances).

issues.label: Alimony amount and duration
issues.why: Court must set amount/duration consistent with statutory factors and evidence.

issues.label: Alimony retroactivity
issues.why: Court must decide whether alimony is retroactive and compute any arrears properly.

issues.label: Alimony tax treatment
issues.why: Court must consider current federal tax law (non-deductible/non-includible) when assessing ability/need.

issues.label: Consideration of marital contributions
issues.why: Court must weigh each spouse’s contributions (career moves, childcare, homemaking, earnings).

issues.label: Effect of part-time work history
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether reduced work was agreed/child-related and how it affects earning capacity.

issues.label: Temporary noncontribution claim
issues.why: Court must resolve dispute over whether husband stopped household contributions and resulting equitable remedies.

issues.label: Credits for post-separation payments
issues.why: Court must decide credits/offsets for payments of household, child, or medical expenses after separation.

issues.label: Equitable distribution required
issues.why: Court must identify, value, and distribute marital assets and liabilities equitably.

issues.label: Marital vs nonmarital classification
issues.why: Court must classify each asset/debt (including separate accounts) as marital or nonmarital.

issues.label: Valuation date(s)
issues.why: Court must select appropriate valuation dates for assets and liabilities.

issues.label: Treatment of separate bank accounts
issues.why: Court must assess whether separate accounts contain marital funds and whether tracing is required.

issues.label: Joint account accounting
issues.why: Court must determine contributions, withdrawals, and whether credits are due for unequal funding.

issues.label: Five-million asset pool division
issues.why: Court must ensure distribution is equitable and supported by findings given substantial assets.

issues.label: Investment and retirement accounts
issues.why: Court must address division/valuation of retirement, brokerage, and any deferred compensation.

issues.label: Stock/RSU/bonus deferrals
issues.why: Court must determine whether employer equity/deferrals are marital and how to value/divide them.

issues.label: Marital home disposition
issues.why: Court must decide exclusive use, sale, buyout, and allocation of expenses/credits for the home.

issues.label: Household expense sufficiency dispute
issues.why: Court must resolve factual dispute about whether joint contributions covered expenses and consequences for credits.

issues.label: Tax liabilities allocation
issues.why: Court must allocate any marital tax debts/refunds and account for 2021 payment from joint funds.

issues.label: 2021 joint tax payment characterization
issues.why: Court must determine whether payment was marital and how it affects equitable distribution.

issues.label: Attorney’s fees and costs
issues.why: Court may need to address fee entitlement based on need/ability and litigation conduct.

issues.label: Findings of fact sufficiency
issues.why: Final judgment must contain adequate findings to permit appellate review on support, alimony, and parenting issues.

issues.label: Standard of review implications
issues.why: Issues on appeal depend on whether errors are factual vs legal and the deference owed.

issues.label: Preservation of factual challenges
issues.why: Failure to move for rehearing may bar appellate review of inadequate factual findings.

issues.label: Preservation of legal errors
issues.why: Pure legal errors (e.g., guideline misapplication) may remain reviewable without rehearing.

issues.label: Rehearing requirement for missing findings
issues.why: Appellate rules/cases may require rehearing to challenge lack of required findings.

issues.label: Effect of amended final judgment
issues.why: Court must confirm what was modified and whether amendments cured or created errors.

issues.label: Effective date of final support orders
issues.why: Court must specify commencement dates for ongoing child support and any alimony obligations.

issues.label: Termination events
issues.why: Court must specify statutory termination triggers (majority, emancipation, death, etc.) for child support/alimony.

issues.label: Life insurance security
issues.why: Court must decide whether to require life insurance to secure child support or alimony.

issues.label: COBRA/medical coverage for spouse
issues.why: Court may need to address continuation of health coverage post-dissolution and cost allocation if requested.

issues.label: Parent communication and dispute resolution
issues.why: Parenting plan should address communication, exchanges, and dispute resolution mechanisms.

issues.label: Relocation/travel considerations
issues.why: Given international history, court may need to address potential relocation or travel provisions if raised.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: Court must resolve conflicting testimony on contributions, expenses, and support-related payments.

issues.label: Evidence support for income figures
issues.why: Court must ensure income findings are supported by W-2s, affidavits, and testimony.

issues.label: Consistency with temporary order
issues.why: Court must reconcile final child support with prior temporary order and explain material differences.

issues.label: Arrears payment schedule
issues.why: Court must set any schedule/method for paying remaining arrears consistent with ability to pay.

issues.label: Interest on arrears
issues.why: Court must decide whether statutory interest applies to support arrears and calculate if required.

issues.label: Enforcement and contempt clarity
issues.why: Orders must be sufficiently clear and specific to be enforceable.
